title: How the definition was diluted
text: Veganism was defined by Leslie Cross in 1951 as the doctrine that man should live without exploiting animals. The founders never redefined it. Everything that followed was distortion. In 1957 the definition disappeared from the Society's constitution. In the sixties the movement was recentred from the animal to the practitioner: lifestyle, health, environmental stewardship. The victim disappeared. In 1975 Peter Singer replaced exploitation with suffering as the moral threshold, so use became acceptable if painless. Then, in 1979, came the fatal redefinition, with three insertions: as far as is possible and practicable, the escape clause; cruelty to, alongside exploitation; and the benefit of humans, animals and the environment. By 2010 the plant-based rebrand had removed the ethical content altogether. The animals were the only reason the word existed. The founders never redefined it. You are here to fix it.
